pll2d15c4-d1e3519.summary: Asks whether some tiny creatures were created in the first creation or arose later from decaying things (Augustine).

pll2d15c4-d1e3531.summary: Answers that many arise from moist bodies, exhalations, corpses, or rotting wood, plants, and fruits, and God is author of all. Those from animal bodies, especially dead, were created with the animals only potentially and materially; those from earth, waters, or what the earth produced can fittingly be said created then.
claims: Creatures from decay were created potentially.
God is author of all creatures.

pl-l2d15c4.summary: Asks whether small creatures arising from decay were made in the first creation or arose later. Many arise from moist bodies, exhalations, corpses, or rotting wood and plants, and God is author of all. Those arising from animal bodies, especially dead ones, were created with the animals only potentially and materially; those arising from earth, water, or plants can be said to have been created then (Augustine).
claims: Many small creatures arise from decay.
God is author of all of them.
Those from animal bodies were created only potentially and materially.
Those from earth, water, or plants can be said to have been created at first.
